holidays.name: National Bacon Day
holidays.description: A salute to the crispy, smoky, sizzling strip that has taken over breakfast tables, burgers, and even desserts. Fry up a batch, wrap something in it, or put it on a maple donut. Today is the day to do it.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance. Its creator is unclear, and it has been listed on December 30 calendars for years as a way to end the year on a savory note.
holidays.funFact: Bacon is one of the oldest preserved meats. People were curing pork belly in China as far back as around 1500 BCE.

holidays.name: Falling Needles Family Fest Day
holidays.description: This holiday is for the post-Christmas moment when the tree starts shedding. Families gather to enjoy the last of the holiday season, needles and all. It's a chance to laugh about the pine-scented mess and sweep up together.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It appears to be a lighthearted way to stretch the holiday cheer until New Year's.
holidays.funFact: A fresh-cut tree can drop a surprising number of needles once it dries out. Keeping the stand full of water slows the shedding noticeably.

holidays.name: National Bicarbonate of Soda Day
holidays.description: A day to appreciate baking soda, the humble white powder in your pantry. It makes pancakes fluffy and fridges fresher. It also soothes heartburn and scrubs stubborn pots clean.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It celebrates the household staple's many uses in the kitchen and around the home.
holidays.funFact: Baking soda makes baked goods rise by reacting with an acid, such as buttermilk or lemon juice, to release bubbles of carbon dioxide gas.
